zh.title: 美國陸軍撤回沖繩下地島機場使用申請，兩架MH-47G直升機改直接前往嘉手納基地
zh.summary: 沖繩縣11月23日表示，美軍已撤回宮古島市下地島機場的使用申請。美國陸軍原申報當天下午以兩架 MH-47G 直升機在該機場加油；日本媒體報導，機場管理事務所當天接獲通知，直升機不前往下地島，改往嘉手納基地。
body: 沖繩縣11月23日表示，美軍已撤回宮古島市下地島機場的使用申請。《沖繩時報》報導，下地島機場管理事務所接獲的通知內容為「不前往下地島，將前往嘉手納基地」。《琉球新報》報導，為美軍提供航務等支援的民間公司在當天下午4時左右，向機場管理事務所通知取消使用；該報刊出的照片說明顯示，美國陸軍 MH-47G 直升機於當天下午5時11分飛抵嘉手納基地。
《琉球新報》另報導，原定使用的下地島機場當天有反對民眾集會抗議，包含來自縣外的參加者在內，共20餘人到場。
依《沖繩時報》等日本媒體先前報導，美國陸軍在日期為11月16日的文件中向沖繩縣申報，將於11月23日使用下地島機場，目的為加油；申報時段為日本時間下午4時30分至5時30分，使用的是兩架 MH-47G 直升機。琉球朝日放送報導，這兩架直升機據信隸屬日本境外的美軍基地。
下地島機場由沖繩縣管理。沖繩電視臺報導，依1971年琉球政府與日本政府簽署的「屋良覺書」及1979年的「西銘確認書」，該機場原則上僅供民航機使用。《沖繩時報》先前指出，若美軍依申報使用，將是扣除緊急降落後，自2006年以來、相隔20年的首次。
沖繩縣在申報後已向美國陸軍及日美相關機關要求自制。琉球朝日放送報導，縣方在要求中表示「平時應避免經常性使用民用機場」。《宮古新報》報導，宮古島市長嘉數登也發表意見，表示對民航以外的使用，除緊急情況外要求自制的立場不變。
《沖繩時報》11月23日的社論另指出，直升機自菲律賓飛來，原定加油後前往嘉手納基地；美軍原先申報使用宮古機場，因無法在希望的時段使用而改為下地島機場。該報並引述沖繩縣知事古謝玄太表示，顧慮對縣民生活、事業活動的影響及心理負擔，美方應避免使用。
沖繩電視臺與《宮古新報》報導，美國海軍陸戰隊2023年也曾以訓練為由申報使用下地島機場，後來未使用。

en.title: US Army withdraws filing to refuel two MH-47G helicopters at Okinawa's Shimojishima Airport (SHI); aircraft head to Kadena instead
en.summary: Okinawa Prefecture said on November 23 that the US military had withdrawn its application to use Shimojishima Airport in Miyakojima. The US Army had filed to refuel two MH-47G helicopters there that afternoon; Japanese media report that the airport office was told the helicopters would not go to Shimojishima and would head to Kadena Air Base.
body: Okinawa Prefecture said on November 23 that the US military had withdrawn its application to use Shimojishima Airport (SHI) in Miyakojima. The Okinawa Times reported that the airport's management office was told the helicopters would not go to Shimojishima and would head to Kadena Air Base. According to the Ryukyu Shimpo, a private company that supports US military flight operations notified the airport office of the cancellation at around 4 p.m. that day; the newspaper's photo caption shows a US Army MH-47G arriving at Kadena Air Base at 5:11 p.m.
The Ryukyu Shimpo also reported that people opposed to the use held a protest that day at Shimojishima Airport, with a little over 20 taking part, including some from outside the prefecture.

As the Okinawa Times and other Japanese media reported earlier, the US Army notified Okinawa Prefecture, in a filing dated November 16, that it would use Shimojishima Airport on November 23 for refuelling. The filing covered 4:30 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. Japan time and two MH-47G helicopters. Ryukyu Asahi Broadcasting reported that the helicopters are believed to belong to a US base outside Japan.

Shimojishima Airport is managed by Okinawa Prefecture. Okinawa Television reported that under the 1971 Yara memorandum between the then Ryukyu government and the Japanese government, and the 1979 Nishime confirmation, the airport is in principle used only by civil aircraft. Had the use gone ahead as filed, it would have been the first by the US military since 2006, excluding emergency landings, the Okinawa Times said before the planned date.

After the filing, the prefecture asked the US Army and Japanese and US authorities to refrain. Ryukyu Asahi Broadcasting reported that the request said routine use of civil airports in peacetime should be avoided. Miyakojima Mayor Noboru Kakazu also issued a comment saying the city's position of asking for restraint on non-civil use, except in emergencies, has not changed, the Miyako Shinpo reported.

An Okinawa Times editorial on November 23 added that the helicopters were flying in from the Philippines and had been due to continue to Kadena Air Base after refuelling, and that the US military had first filed to use Miyako Airport (MMY) before switching to Shimojishima when its preferred time slot was unavailable. It quoted Okinawa Governor Genta Koja as saying the US side should refrain because of concern about the effect on residents' lives and business activity and the psychological burden.
Okinawa Television and the Miyako Shinpo reported that the US Marine Corps also filed to use Shimojishima Airport for training in 2023 and did not go ahead.

facts.claim: Okinawa Prefecture said on November 23 that the US military had withdrawn its application to use Shimojishima Airport, where two MH-47G helicopters had been due that evening; the airport management office was told they would not go to Shimojishima and would head to Kadena Air Base.

A private company supporting US military flight operations notified the Shimojishima Airport management office of the cancellation at around 4 p.m. on November 23; a photo caption shows a US Army MH-47G arriving at Kadena Air Base at 5:11 p.m. that day.
People opposed to the use protested at Shimojishima Airport on November 23; a little over 20 took part, including some from outside the prefecture.

The US Army notified Okinawa Prefecture, in a filing dated November 16, that it would use Shimojishima Airport on November 23 for refuelling; the prefecture asked Japanese and US authorities to refrain; it would be the first US military use since 2006 excluding emergency landings.
The filing covers 4:30 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. on November 23 and two MH-47G helicopters.
The helicopters are believed to belong to a US base outside Japan, and the prefecture's request said routine peacetime use of civil airports should be avoided.

The 1971 Yara memorandum and the 1979 Nishime confirmation provide that the airport is in principle used only by civil aircraft; the US Marine Corps filed to use it for training in 2023 and did not go ahead.
Miyakojima Mayor Noboru Kakazu said the city's position of asking for restraint on non-civil use except in emergencies has not changed.
The helicopters were flying in from the Philippines and would go on to Kadena Air Base; the US military first filed for Miyako Airport; Governor Genta Koja said the US side should refrain.
